$comment: RFC-0028. The loop with the worst reversibility profile: a design mistake surfaces months later in code nobody wants to unwind. That is why its gate is a panel, not a script.
name: design
description: Take a ratified requirement to a recorded architectural decision — constraints, structure, diagrams, threats, then a panel that must agree before the decision is written down. Use when the user is designing a system, choosing an architecture, or asking how something should be built.

stages.intent: Name the quality targets before the structure, so the design is judged against numbers rather than taste.
Write the design and render it. The prose and the picture are one artifact and must not disagree.
Attack the design that now exists, before it is ratified rather than after it is built.
A standing panel takes independent positions before cross-talk, surfaces the cruxes, and records dissent.
Write the decision down with its rejected alternatives, so the next team inherits the reasoning and not just the outcome.
